source_name: MKIK – Modern Vállalkozások Program 2.0 project page (DIMOP_Plusz-1.2.7-23-2023-00001)
why_relevant: Names the exact project code, consortium and operator behind the accreditation catalogue, giving the governance chain (who decides which vendors qualify) and linking chamber, KIFÜ and ministry actors.

source_name: KIFÜ (Kormányzati Informatikai Fejlesztési Ügynökség) – EU project pages
why_relevant: State IT development agency that is beneficiary/implementer of large DIMOP/KÖFOP digitalisation projects; its project pages disclose scope and often consortium partners and suppliers of government digital infrastructure that payment vendors integrate with.

source_name: Magyar Államkincstár – EU-funded (DIMOP Plusz / KÖFOP) project disclosures
why_relevant: The Treasury and NAV are core state financial-infrastructure beneficiaries; their mandatory project disclosure pages give code, support amount (e.g. HUF 9bn for the complex legal-relationship register), start date and functional scope — direct evidence of state payment/registry IT demand.

source_name: NAV – DIMOP Plusz / EU-financed projects section
why_relevant: Tax authority digitalisation projects (online invoicing, e-receipt/e-nyugta, registers) directly shape POS, cash-register and payment-data requirements for merchants and their suppliers; the EU-project pages state scope and funding.

source_name: EU Cohesion Open Data Platform
why_relevant: Programme-level allocations and spend for Hungary 2021-2027 by fund, programme, policy objective and intervention field (incl. digitalisation fields). Gives the size of the money pool behind each digitalisation line and how fast it is being absorbed — context for sizing addressable subsidised demand, not individual winners.

source_name: European Commission – Hungary's Recovery and Resilience Plan country page (Reforms & Investments portal)
why_relevant: Authoritative measure-by-measure description of Hungary's RRF plan (including the July 2026 revised plan agreed by Council), with the digital component's investments, milestones and targets. Defines what public digitalisation work is contractually obliged to happen and by when.

source_name: Recovery and Resilience Scoreboard (incl. Hungary country overview and digital transformation view)
why_relevant: Tracks fulfilment status of Hungary's milestones/targets and disbursements, including the digital-expenditure view. Tells you which digitalisation investments are actually progressing versus stalled — a timing signal for when supplier contracts appear.

source_name: European Commission State Aid Transparency Public Search (TAM)
why_relevant: Every individual aid award above the reporting threshold (EUR 500k) must be published with beneficiary name, sector (NACE), region, aid instrument, amount range and granting authority. For Hungary this exposes large subsidies to financial-sector and IT companies that may never surface in the national project search, including aid to private beneficiaries.

source_name: MFB Zrt. – MFB Pont Plusz intermediary network and GINOP Plusz combined loan programmes
source_subtype: state development bank – financial intermediary list and programme terms
why_relevant: GINOP Plusz combined instruments (e.g. 1.4.3-24, 1.4.4-24, 1.4.5-25 'Nemzeti Bajnokok' green & digital transition loan) are delivered only through MFB-contracted intermediaries; MFB publishes the intermediary list. This maps which banks distribute subsidised digitalisation finance — a partnership and channel map of the Hungarian banking sector around EU money.

source_name: EUPR / EPTK (FAIR) application system help centre – Támogatott projekt kereső documentation
why_relevant: Documents the underlying data plumbing: the supported-project search draws on EMIR, EUPR and IIER with daily updates. Essential for judging data freshness, field semantics and how to query the system reliably; also names the EPTK/FAIR ecosystem where beneficiaries file claims.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – GINOP project disclosure page
why_relevant: Demonstrates that banking-sector bodies themselves are EU grant beneficiaries and must publish project descriptions; the Banking Association's own GINOP project page is a concrete case and a hub for further sector actors.

source_name: NFSZ / munka.hu – GINOP Plusz-3.2.2-24 flagship project page (employment IT system replacement, consortium with NISZ Zrt.)
why_relevant: Example of a 'kiemelt' (flagship, non-competitive) grant that names the consortium — ministry, county government offices and NISZ Zrt. — and the objective of replacing a legacy state IT system. Flagship-project pages are where large state IT integrator roles become visible early.

source_name: Neumann János Nonprofit Kft. (NTP) – project portfolio
source_subtype: state nonprofit implementing body project list
why_relevant: Ministry background institution running national data-economy and digitalisation programmes (NATUK and successors) largely on EU funds; its project list reveals state-driven digital initiatives and partner ecosystems adjacent to payments and digital identity.

source_name: Hungarian grant-consultancy and pályázat trade press (pafi.hu, palyaz.hu, dft.hu, nphprojekt.hu, palyazatnet.hu, bkik.hu)
source_subtype: trade/consultancy aggregators and mirrors of call documents
why_relevant: Consultancies republish draft and final call texts, product sheets and eligibility analyses faster and more legibly than the official portal, and often host felhívás PDF versions that later disappear. Good early-warning layer for new digitalisation calls; must be treated as secondary and validated against palyazat.gov.hu.

source_name: Hungarian business press EU-funds desks (Világgazdaság, Portfolio, Pénzcentrum) – award decisions and beneficiary lists
why_relevant: Publishes government award decisions with named beneficiary lists and aggregate absorption figures (e.g. reporting on tens of billions of HUF awarded in a single day, and on unblocked RRF funds for digitalisation) often before the official register updates. Useful for timing and for narrative context around who wins.

source_name: eGov Hírlevél – RRF / e-government funding tag
why_relevant: Specialist Hungarian e-government newsletter that tracks publicly funded digitalisation projects, including identity, registry and payment-adjacent state systems, with links back to primary documents — a useful curated pointer layer for this cell.

source_name: Finextra Research — Hungary coverage (news + vendor press releases)
source_subtype: international specialist trade media / vendor press-release wire
why_relevant: Finextra carries both editorial news and verbatim vendor press releases about Hungarian bank technology selections (Diebold/Erste Bank Hungary ATM bill payment, ACI Worldwide with OTP Bank and Erste Bank Hungary for instant payments/open banking, Nets winning the Hungarian instant payments contract, UniCredit Hungary–Alipay, Barion acquisition). The press-release channel often carries vendor-supplied product/scope detail that Hungarian outlets omit.

source_name: The Paypers — payments/fintech news and country/regional analysis
why_relevant: Covers acquiring, PSP and marketplace partnerships touching Hungary (e.g. Revolut–Pepita one-click payments/acquiring in CEE) and publishes recurring global fintech M&A analyses and CEE expert views that name Hungarian actors. Has an on-site search facility usable as a pointer into partner/vendor announcements.

source_name: IBS Intelligence (IBSi) — news and vendor case studies
source_subtype: analyst house + trade media + case-study library
why_relevant: Analyst-plus-media hybrid: publishes deal news on Hungarian core-banking and payments implementations (OTP Bank implementing iGCB Intellect Digital Core and Lending) and hosts vendor case studies specific to OTP real-time payments. IBSi Sales League Table / rankings are a rare public proxy for vendor win counts in CEE.

source_name: Retail Banker International (GlobalData media)
why_relevant: Retail-banking trade title reporting Hungarian bank technology and product moves (OTP Bank deploying Intellect Digital Core; OTP mobile payment service launch with Cellum/Mastercard). Part of the GlobalData stable, so articles frequently cite GlobalData market data — a bridge between news and analyst sizing.

source_name: PYMNTS.com — Hungary instant/real-time payments coverage
why_relevant: US-based payments media that contextualises Hungarian instant payments (AFR/GIROInstant) for an international audience and republishes analyst volume forecasts (e.g. Hungary real-time payments volume growth to 2026 drawing on ACI/GlobalData Prime Time data) that no Hungarian outlet packages the same way.

source_name: FinTech Futures — Hungary keyword feed
why_relevant: Maintains a country keyword page aggregating all Hungary-tagged banking-technology stories (e.g. OTP Bank taps iGCB for core banking revamp), which is effectively a ready-made longitudinal deal feed for the market.

source_name: GlobalData Report Store — Hungary Cards and Payments
why_relevant: The canonical paid country market-sizing report ('Hungary Cards and Payments: Opportunities and Risks to 2030'): card/cash/credit-transfer/direct-debit values, e-commerce sizing, issuer and scheme shares. Free abstract pages leak headline figures and table-of-contents structure useful even without purchase.

source_name: Euromonitor International — Financial Cards and Payments in Hungary
why_relevant: Consumer-finance angle on the Hungarian card market with brand/issuer shares and channel splits; separate sub-reports for credit cards and charge cards. Complements GlobalData for triangulating card-base and transaction-value estimates.

source_name: Mordor Intelligence — Hungary POS Terminal Market (+ companies page)
source_subtype: commercial analyst market report (syndicated, lower rigour)
why_relevant: Directly on-target for a POS/terminal vendor: publicly visible summary gives CAGR and, critically, a named competitor list for the Hungarian POS terminal market (Worldline SA, NovoPayment, SRS Informatika Kft., B-Payment Szolgáltató Zrt., Quadrapay) — i.e. a free actor map for the acquiring/terminal layer.

source_name: Statista — Hungary digital payments / fintech market outlook
why_relevant: Modelled market outlook (transaction value, users, segment splits for digital commerce and mobile POS) plus survey-derived Hungarian consumer statistics on card acceptance and contactless usage. Useful for quick framing and slide-ready numbers; the modelling is derivative, so treat as secondary.

source_name: MarketResearch.com — Hungary banking/cards report aggregator
why_relevant: Reseller catalogue that enumerates which publishers have Hungary-specific banking, cards and payments reports and when they were refreshed — an efficient way to discover analyst houses covering Hungary without querying each one, and to detect new report releases.

source_name: Research and Markets — Mordor and multi-publisher Hungary listings
why_relevant: Second large report reseller; its publisher pages and country filters surface Hungary payments/POS/banking titles from many houses, with abstracts that often disclose segment definitions and named vendors.
